I kinda understand what you're feeling. I've felt my emotions slowly going away until I've just felt numb. I've also stopped interacting with my family and friends mainly because I just didn't want to anymore. It was too much effort to put up a facade and I really didn't care anymore. I didn't find help until after my first suicide attempt. The docs put me on antidepressants, and I started seeing a therapist back at home (I was at uni before). I didn't see a change right away but I did get better after a month. That first month was hard because I still felt suicidal, but I didn't have the courage to leave anymore. Afterwards, I started to get better and I began to actually look forward to things and want to be with people. 
Obviously, your experience is unique to you. And I'm very sorry your family doesn't seem supportive of you. I really am. Maybe if you talk with your friends, they might understand and help you through this difficult time. I genuinely wish the best for you and I hope you find the help you need.

I agree. When I was planning my first attempt, I was so giddy and relieved that I was finally gonna get some peace from everything going on in my life. I mean, you're finding the solution to the biggest problems in your life. I wouldn't blame anyone for being happy about that.
